records.source: Reuters / Joe Cash and John Geddie / Chinese smart ports
records.claim: China's transport ministry reports 60 domestic automated terminals with a target of 90 by 2030; Qingdao Qianwan terminal reports 61 containers per crane-hour; China Merchants Port cited existing overseas terminal software deployments and Beijing proposed work on electronic bills of lading.
records.observation: Reported statistics, company filings and proposals; does not demonstrate new 10 Nov commissioning or Chinese operational control over global shipping.

records.source: Reuters commentary / Gavin Maguire / European flexible electricity
records.claim: LSEG data in Reuters commentary indicate German wind output below seasonal norms since late October, Nordic hydro at multi-year lows and Danube basin hydro weakness, with gas generation increasingly balancing the German grid.
records.observation: Analytical commentary with referenced LSEG series; no single new measured 10 Nov capacity-loss event or universal storage requirement established.

records.source: Reuters / Enes Tunagur / oil risk premium and Hormuz
records.claim: As of 09:30 GMT, Brent traded at $90.18 after briefly falling below $90; WTI $84.74. The report attributes repricing to prospects of U.S. restraint, oversupply concerns and continued shipping security risks.
records.observation: Intraday price quotation and attributed political statements; neither an independent ship-transit series nor verified reopening.
records.assessment: MARKET EVIDENCE — NOT CONFIRMED PHYSICAL FLOW CHANGE

records.claim: Reuters investigation found international retreat of China's LOGINK logistics-data platform, failed/stalled partnerships and operational difficulties despite previous ambitions.
records.observation: Background published October 5, not a November 10 event; important counterevidence against equating overseas port hardware with integrated data control.
records.assessment: CONTRARY BACKGROUND — NO UNIFIED WORLDWIDE DATA PLATFORM
